lineRule: One item is one physical line without LF/CRLF terminator, or a whole-unit part of an oversized line. Bare CR is text. bytes includes the consumed terminator on the final part; it is a source-byte count, not decoded UTF-8 text length.
continuedRule: continued is true on all non-final parts of the same physical line and false on its last part. A running unterminated suffix is withheld until LF/CRLF, terminal EOF, or enough lookahead proves another nonempty part follows. No zero-byte closure items are emitted.
ordering: Per-stream byte order only. Each poll reads at most one 64 KiB backend page per stream and emits stdout parts before stderr parts, within item/page limits; a deferred stream keeps its offset. There is no recoverable chronological interleave between separate stdout/stderr artifacts. PTY uses only stream pty in its combined capture order.
nextRule: next is non-null while running, even when the page is empty. Reading it later resumes from the stream offsets and can observe appended bytes. next is null only after terminal status and both streams are fully drained. No total.
cursorOffsets: original once a durable per-stream prefix base exists; legacy unknown-origin cursors must remain explicitly unknown/retained-relative and never claim original zero
startRule: No cursor starts at original zero on an untrimmed stream, or at the first available original offset after a trim. Each item repeats that stream firstAvailableOffset/prefixDropped; the page must not label a retained tail as original line 1.

retention.method: atomic UTF-8-aligned tail replacement; no promise to keep the beginning

storageDependency: The later bash_output/storage slice must durably initialize and maintain each stream cumulative dropped-prefix base in the task record at every trim, preserving it across restart and accumulating further removals. Cursor offsets are original offsets; clamp unread positions below the retained base to that base. Legacy tasks trimmed before tracking may use null only with prefixDropped true. Never emit base zero for a trimmed stream.
